To: Angela Ruiz
From: Nolan Pierce
Subject: Designer recommendation
Date: March 12
Dear Angela,
You asked last week whether I knew a reliable graphic designer for your product catalog, and I am glad to recommend Curtis Holloway.
Curtis spent several years at Brookmere Creative Agency before opening his own practice. When I asked why he had struck out on his own, he explained that what he valued most was sitting down directly with the local business owners he served, rather than routing every decision through account managers. That focus is clear in how he operates today. He works almost entirely with small companies in our region, and he takes on several kinds of projects, including logos, printed brochures, and graphics for websites.
If you decide to reach out, Curtis offers a first meeting at no cost, so you can describe your project and view samples of his earlier work before committing to anything. You do not need to book weeks in advance, and the meeting is open to anyone considering his services, not only first-time clients. Once a project begins, he usually delivers the finished files within two weeks.
I engaged Curtis myself last quarter for our conference materials, and I was impressed from start to finish. When the completed booklet reached my supervisor, Ms. Loretta Vance, she was delighted with the result and asked who had produced it. That reaction alone should tell you a great deal about the quality of his work.
Please feel free to mention my name when you contact him. I am confident you will find him easy to work with, and I would be happy to answer any further questions.
Best regards,
Nolan Pierce

Calderwood Timepieces Receives Northfield Design Prize
Award announced alongside the launch of a new collection
HAVENPORT, March 3, 2024 — Calderwood Timepieces reported today that it has received the Northfield Design Prize, an honor given each year by the Institute of Industrial Design to a single watch manufacturer. The judges praised the clean lines and lasting build of the company's Voyage model, noting in particular its clear, easy-to-read dial.
Founder Harriet Osei, who has personally overseen every watch design since she opened the company five years ago, said that the prize reflects the effort of the entire workshop rather than any single person.
Calderwood introduced its very first model in the year it opened, and that watch still sells steadily today. This month the company adds a new collection led by the Nocturne, its most recent design. As with every Calderwood wristwatch, the new models are designed and manufactured in-house, and the complete range is carried by retailers across the country.

Willowbank Weekend Makers Market — Vendor Participation Program
The following terms apply to every vendor at the Willowbank Weekend Makers Market and remain in effect throughout the year.
The market exists to give makers a place to sell their own work. For this reason, every item offered for sale must be handmade by the vendor who presents it, and goods bought for resale or produced in a factory may not be sold.
No single stall may be wider than three meters. Because the market supplies neither tables nor weather coverings, vendors must bring their own.
Anyone who wishes to take part should make sure that a completed application form reaches the market office at least two weeks before the season opens. First-time vendors are exempt from the usual booth fee of twenty-five dollars. Once approved, vendors receive a stipend of forty dollars for every market day they attend. Trading takes place on Saturdays and Sundays only.
Questions may be sent to the Willowbank Market Office at
[email protected]
.

Please let me know whether you would be willing to be featured.
Theodore Marsh
Vendor Relations, Willowbank Market Office
Replies are answered Monday to Thursday.
